UK CRYPTO CGT CALCULATOR · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

What does HMRC say you sold?

Paste your crypto buys, sales, swaps and staking income as a CSV. The calculator applies HMRC's same-day rule, 30-day rule and Section 104 pool to every disposal, shows which rule matched each one, and estimates each tax year's capital gains tax after the exempt amount. Download the working to keep with your records.

Arithmetic on figures you supply. Not legal, tax, or financial advice. New to the rules? Read Section 104 pooling for crypto, with a worked example.

Your transactions

Columns: date, type, asset, quantity, gbp value, fee; swaps also to asset, to quantity. Types: buy, sell, income, swap, donate. Dates as 2024-05-02 or 02/05/2024 (day first). Put the pound value of the whole row in gbp value, not the price per unit.

Paste or open your transactions, then click Work out my gains.

Every disposal and the rule that matched it

Section 104 pools at the end of each tax year

Income received as crypto

What this does and does not cover

  • Covered: purchases, sales, swaps between assets, staking and airdrop receipts entered at their pound value, charity donations, fees, losses carried between years, the exempt amount and the rate change on 30 October 2024.
  • Not covered: DeFi and liquidity pools, NFTs, forks, wrapped tokens, lost or stolen coins, gifts to a spouse (no gain, no loss) or to others, income tax on staking, trading-income treatment, and transfers between your own wallets (leave them out of the file; they are not disposals).
  • Prices are yours. Nothing is fetched, so a missing pound value is skipped and reported, never guessed as zero.

Questions

What is the Section 104 pool for crypto?

HMRC treats all units of one cryptoasset as a single pool. Every purchase adds its units and allowable cost to the pool, and a disposal uses a share of the pool's cost in proportion to the units sold. It is an average cost, not first-in first-out, and you cannot pick which coins you sold.

What are the same-day and 30-day rules?

Before the pool is used, a disposal is matched with units of the same asset you bought on the same day, then with units you bought in the 30 days after the disposal, earliest first. Selling and buying back within 30 days therefore does not create a loss you can claim from the old pool.

Which fees can I deduct?

Fees paid to buy count towards the cost of the units. Fees paid to sell or swap come off the proceeds. Enter each fee in pounds in the fee column.

Is a crypto-to-crypto swap taxable in the UK?

Yes. Swapping one cryptoasset for another is a disposal of the first, at its pound value on the day. This tool treats a swap row as a disposal of the asset you gave up and an acquisition of the one you received at the same pound value.

How is staking or airdrop income treated here?

Income rows are added to the pool at their pound value when received, so a later sale has the right cost. The income itself may also be taxable as income and is listed separately; this tool does not work out income tax.

Which tax years and rates are built in?

2021-22 to 2026-27: the annual exempt amount for each year, and the capital gains rates for crypto, including the change on 30 October 2024 from 10% and 20% to 18% and 24%. Check the figures against HMRC before you file, because the 2026-27 row assumes the 2025-26 rules continue.

Is my transaction history uploaded?

No. The page runs in your browser, reads the file on your device and sends nothing anywhere.

Can I use the result on my tax return?

Use it as working, not as advice. It does not cover every case, for example DeFi, NFTs, forks, transfers between your own wallets that you have not removed, gifts to a spouse, or losses claimed outside the file. Check the result against HMRC's guidance or with an adviser.

No warranty. This tool is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It is not legal, tax, or financial advice and does not replace an adviser or HMRC's guidance. Results are arithmetic on the figures you type; tax rules, rates and reporting requirements change. You are responsible for reviewing and verifying its output before you file anything.

Independent. Not affiliated with HMRC, any exchange, wallet, blockchain or crypto tax software, and none is ranked here. The example transactions are invented.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you enter, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record — nothing you enter is saved anywhere.

Everything runs in your browser. Your transactions are never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (analysis_run, example_loaded, file_opened, report_downloaded) are counted only in local storage on your device, never with any of your data, and are switched off by Do Not Track.

Related tools: the UK capital gains tax calculator for shares and property, the UK self assessment tax calculator, and the US-rules crypto cost basis calculator (FIFO, HIFO, Form 8949).

Free and open source. If this helped, the code is under an MIT licence — support is entirely optional and never changes what the tool does.

UK Crypto CGT Calculator · guide

Section 104 pooling for crypto: a worked UK example

If you bought Bitcoin more than once, HMRC does not let you say which coins you sold. It treats all your units of one cryptoasset as a single pool and, before touching the pool, checks two shorter rules. This page works one example in pounds. The calculator runs the same arithmetic on your own file.

The order HMRC matches a disposal

  1. Same day. Units of the same asset you bought on the day you sold.
  2. The next 30 days. Units you bought in the 30 days after the sale, earliest first. This stops you selling to claim a loss and buying straight back.
  3. The Section 104 pool. Everything else comes out of one pool at its average allowable cost.

The example

All numbers are invented. Fees are in pounds. A fee on a purchase adds to its cost; a fee on a sale comes off the proceeds.

DateWhatBTCPoundsFee
10 Jun 2021Buy0.515,00020
20 Jan 2022Buy0.310,50015
2 May 2024Sell0.419,20025
2 May 2024Buy0.16,20010
11 Nov 2024Sell0.214,00018
25 Nov 2024Buy0.1510,20012

The pool before 2024. 0.8 BTC at a cost of £15,020 + £10,515 = £25,535.

2 May 2024. You sold 0.4 BTC for £19,200 less a £25 fee: £19,175, or £47,937.50 a coin. You also bought 0.1 BTC the same day for £6,210 including the fee. So the same-day rule matches 0.1 BTC: proceeds £4,793.75 against cost £6,210, a loss of £1,416.25. The other 0.3 BTC comes from the pool at £25,535 × 0.3 ÷ 0.8 = £9,575.625, against proceeds of £14,381.25, a gain of £4,805.63 (to the penny). The pool is left with 0.5 BTC at £15,959.375. The 0.1 BTC you bought that day never entered the pool.

11 Nov 2024. You sold 0.2 BTC for £13,982 after the fee. You buy 0.15 BTC back on 25 Nov, 14 days later, for £10,212. The 30-day rule matches that 0.15 BTC: proceeds £10,486.50, cost £10,212, a gain of £274.50. The last 0.05 BTC comes from the pool at £15,959.375 × 0.05 ÷ 0.5 = £1,595.94, against proceeds of £3,495.50, a gain of £1,899.56. The bought-back coins are used up and also never enter the pool, which is left with 0.45 BTC at £14,363.44.

Adding it up for 2024-25

The year runs 6 April 2024 to 5 April 2025. In this file the BTC disposals produce gains of £6,979.69 and a loss of £1,416.25; the calculator's sample file adds an ETH-to-SOL swap and a SOL sale for a fuller picture. The annual exempt amount for 2024-25 is £3,000. Gains above it were taxed at 10% or 20% for disposals up to 29 October 2024 and 18% or 24% from 30 October 2024, depending on how much of your basic-rate band your income leaves free.

Where people go wrong

  • Treating each sale as first-in first-out. HMRC's pool is an average, so an old cheap coin does not sit under a new sale.
  • Selling and rebuying within 30 days. The loss you expect is replaced by a match against the repurchase.
  • Forgetting swaps. Swapping one coin for another is a disposal, at the pound value of what you received.
  • Missing purchases. A sale with no matching purchase has no cost, so the gain looks far too large. The calculator warns when that happens.

No warranty. This guide is free and as-is. It is not legal, tax, or financial advice. Rules and rates change; check HMRC's Cryptoassets Manual or an adviser. Not affiliated with HMRC or any exchange.
